content:
elaine-support: Customer on private VPC reporting KMS->HSM failures after last week's network changes. App calls start failing with PKCS11 errors and occasional TLS handshake failures. They see 502s for sign requests. Can someone help triage?

chris-sre: Can you paste the exact error lines and which IP/port the HSM is on? Also did they change any egress allowlists or NAT?

elaine-support: Logs from the KMS proxy: ```
2026-11-02T09:12:01Z ERROR kms.proxy dial tcp 10.10.5.7:1792: connect: connection refused
2026-11-02T09:12:01Z WARN  kms.tls  tls: handshake failure: remote error: tls: bad certificate
2026-11-02T09:12:03Z ERROR kms.sign request_id=abc123 status=502 err="upstream unavailable"
```
Customer also ran: `openssl s_client -connect 10.10.5.7:1792 -servername hsm-vendor.local` and saw `handshake failure` and `no peer certificate`

sachin-eng: Two quick checks: 1) DNS/SNI mismatch — if the HSM expects SNI hsm-vendor.local but the proxy sends kms.internal we get cert verify errors. Check the proxy tls.server_name override. 2) Egress allowlist — vendor rotated hardware last week; they sometimes move to new CIDR blocks.

infra-oncall: Also check for PMTU/fragmentation. We had a similar case where MSS clamping missing on the NAT caused TLS handshake fragments to drop and produced weird timeouts + cert errors. Can you tcpdump on proxy egress and on HSM side? Commands: ```
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 host 10.10.5.7 and port 1792 -w /tmp/hsm.pcap
# from a client in VPC: openssl s_client -connect 10.10.5.7:1792 -servername hsm-vendor.local -brief
```

kms-proxy-bot: Automated note: detected 3 failed connections from customer CIDR 34.210.77.12/32 -> 10.10.5.7:1792 within 5m window. Recent network change: egress ACL updated 2026-11-01 23:04 UTC by infra-team.

elaine-support: Customer confirmed their egress allowlist still had the old vendor IPs (10.10.4.0/24) and vendor moved HSM to 10.10.5.0/24 during maintenance. We asked them to add 10.10.5.0/24:1792 to their allowlist and to validate SNI on the proxy. They did both.

chris-sre: After they added the CIDR, did the tcpdump show a completed TLS handshake?

elaine-support: Yes — tcpdump shows three-way handshake + TLS records, openssl s_client now returns certificate CN=hsm-vendor.local and KMS proxy log shows sign success. Latency is still slightly elevated (~200ms vs 50ms). Customer suspects path through transit gateway.

infra-oncall: If latency persists, check SNAT port exhaustion and route path (transit gateways add hops). Also check MTU on the transit path (jumbo vs 1500). For MTU issues try reducing MSS on the proxy host: `sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1` and add iptables MSS clamp rule on the NAT box.

elaine-support: Customer applied MSS clamping on their NAT and latency dropped to ~70ms. They confirmed full restore of signing pipeline. Marking this as resolved, will follow up with notes for private deployment runbook. :thumbsup:

chris-sre: Nice work. Recommend adding checklist item to support runbook: 1) verify KMS proxy server_name 2) verify egress CIDR + port 1792 3) validate MTU/MSS on transit NAT 4) tcpdump + openssl repro steps.

sachin-eng: I'll draft a quick KB entry and a small diagnostic script that runs the openssl + curl checks and reports common failure signatures.

kms-proxy-bot: Closing note queued: please confirm if you want this thread archived into the private-deploy runbook channel.
